name: a diagnosis is an asserted state; a rule-out is hypothetical and not a diagnosis fact
description: docs/reference/ANALYSIS.md: assertion status gates what counts. A confirmed diagnosis lands as an asserted state on me.diagnosis. A separate 'wants to rule out X' is assertion=hypothetical — it is still recorded (the wiki demotes it) but must NEVER become an asserted diagnosis fact. The absent_facts check pins that no asserted diagnosis exists for the ruled-out condition, while the confirmed diagnosis is present and active.
xfail: TWO accepted gaps, either of which alone fails this file. (1) ACCEPTED, on measurement. assert_fact has no `qualifier` field, so two scalar facts that shared a predicate and differed only in their qualifier collide on one identity key. (Where the qualifier named the OBJECT entity nothing is lost - a non-functional predicate keys on its object.) A `qualifier` field was probed against the live model (evals/shape_probe.py, 12 samples): it filled with prose on 61 of 86 facts - 'previous weight 182 lb in March', 'vehicle no longer owned', 'diagnosed by Dr. Patel' - and left it blank 5 times. An over-applied qualifier SPLITS an identity key, so nothing supersedes ever again; that is strictly worse than the collision it was meant to fix. What ships instead is the channel `registry.decompose_predicate` already read and assert_fact v3 now teaches - `name.nickname.friends` stores as name.nickname + friends - bounded to the five registry predicates declaring a `qualifier_vocab`. A LONG-TAIL qualifier like this one has no such declaration and is still dropped. W5 MUST NOT DELETE: `facts.qualifier`, the identity key that includes it, or `decompose_predicate` and the `qualifier_vocab` declarations it reads. (2) ACCEPTED, on measurement. assert_fact writes assertion='asserted' and has no field for anything else, so a negated, questioned, reported or hypothetical fact cannot be stated at all. Both spellings of a fix were probed against the live model through /api/debug/tool-probe (evals/shape_probe.py, `fields` suite, gpt-oss-120b, 12 samples an arm): an `assertion` STRING whose description names its five words came back legal 0 times in 72 - the model writes the fact's topic (`civic_sold`, `current_weight`, `dana works at everlane`) - and a `negated` BOOLEAN, the one closed vocabulary a tool grammar can carry without an enum (constraint 8), came back false 80 times out of 80, including every time on 'I finally sold the Civic last week so it is gone'. The string fills with garbage, the boolean fills with the majority class and never fires; neither is a channel. The future (`expected`) and past-marker (interval close) normalizers still fire - they are `_upsert_fact`'s own. The surviving channel is the owner's reply: `correct_fact` force-supersedes and pins. W5 MUST NOT DELETE: `facts.assertion` and its CHECK, `supersession.CURRENT_ASSERTIONS` / `_IRREALIS` and the negated-supersedes arm of decide(), or `extraction.ASSERTIONS` - the EMR importer and the reply turn both still write non-asserted rows, and the read surfaces filter on the column.

steps.body: Dr. Okafor confirmed I have type 2 diabetes based on the A1c. Starting metformin.
She also wants to rule out sleep apnea — ordering a sleep study.

facts.statement: Sleep apnea is being investigated (rule out).
